Ukraine Unbroken packs a punch, rising in both power and horror over the course of the evening.
It's after the interval that the evening really takes off.
They are uneven but, together, they are so worthwhile.
Together, these five plays are something more than the sum of their parts.
It's one of those occasions where substance out-performs style, but in a world of ultra-processed disinformation we're all the better for a good bit of geopolitical fibre.
Ukraine Unbroken isn't up to those standards, but you'll leave glad to have seen it.
Ukraine Unbroken is determined to meet the challenge of archiving in real time, and does so with conviction and urgency.
Ukraine Unbroken is an engaging piece of theatre as well as a powerful piece of political commentary.
Although some pieces are lacking in power and refinement, Ukraine Unbroken is a well-structured, emotionally powerful night at the theatre.
By the third playlet – the best of the five – Three Mates by Natalka Vorozhbit, we are 1,468 days into the war, and the enemy is no longer just the one outside dropping bombs on civilians.
The individual plays vary in style and content but give an intriguing and strong presentation of the situation for Ukraine and its people.
